subject: ventures/cache-control-check
professional: a web performance / CDN engineer (Fastly, Cloudflare or Akamai solutions-engineer class) who debugs cache misses against RFC 9111 for a living. First check: for each flagged header combination, does the stated consequence match RFC 9111 (Vary matching in 4.1, validation in 4.3, no-store in 5.2.2.5, s-maxage and Expires precedence in 5.3), and does a danger verdict ever fire when the response is in fact safe, since a false danger fails a CI gate.

evidence.correctness: Ran a local Node http server (scratchpad srv.mjs) serving 11 header sets and ran `node check.mjs` on each. Recomputed against RFC 9111 by hand: (1) /varystar `Vary: *` + max-age=600 -> danger vary-star. Flag is right, but RFC 9111 s4.1 says only that a stored response with `*` 'always fails to match'; s4.3 still lets a cache reuse it after successful validation (ETag/304). The tool and page say 'never reusable' and 'nothing is ever served from cache again', which overstates it (a revalidated 304 is a reuse). (2) /pubnostore `Cache-Control: public, no-store` + Set-Cookie -> tool reports DANGER public-with-set-cookie, exit 1. RFC 9111 s5.2.2.5: no-store forbids a cache storing any part of the response, so no cookie can be replayed; this is a false danger. analyze.test.mjs:203 asserts dangerCount 1 for exactly this input, so the false positive is specified behaviour. (3) /scookie.js `s-maxage=60, public` + past Expires -> notice expires-before-date; RFC 9111 s5.3 gives s-maxage precedence over Expires for shared caches, and the finding's wording ignores that. Correct outputs: /pubcookie (public + 2 cookies -> danger, evidence shows '+1 more'), /nostore (notice), /range (W/ etag + Accept-Ranges: bytes -> notice, matches RFC 9110 13.1.5 If-Range strong-validator rule), /clean (no findings), /exp (Expires 1970 <= Date -> notice, RFC 9111 s4.2.1). Also `Vary: Accept-Encoding, *` is not flagged (strict grammar says * must stand alone, so defensible) and `private="Set-Cookie, X-A"` is split on the quoted comma into a junk directive (harmless here, wrong parser).
evidence.completeness: README claims checked end to end: Vary:* finding (works), public+Set-Cookie (works), no-store+max-age (works), Expires overridden by max-age (unit-tested; fires), Expires<=Date (works), weak ETag + range (works), static asset w/o headers (works on /app.js), CLI exit code 0/1 (verified 0 and 1), --json flag, --timeout, browser page index.html + JSON paste, usage opt-out. 75 tests pass. No stubs or TODOs found; the three vs-/why- SEO pages exist. Not claimed and not present: redirects are reported as-is (documented). `--json` output omits findings by design (page re-analyses). All claimed features work.
evidence.verification: `node --test *.test.mjs` in the venture: 75 pass, 0 fail (0.6 s). Seeded mutation 1 in analyze.mjs: `expiresMs <= dateMs` -> `<`; 1 test failed (caught). Seeded mutation 2: suppress public-with-set-cookie when no-store is present (the correct RFC behaviour); 1 test failed, i.e. the suite pins the false positive. Both reverted from a saved copy; `git status` on the directory is clean. Gaps: probe.mjs network behaviour is tested with stubs/local server only; no test for quoted-comma Cache-Control, s-maxage, or Vary lists containing *.
evidence.craft: Read analyze.mjs, check.mjs, probe.mjs, usage.mjs and their tests. Good: pure classifier shared by CLI and page, promise that always resolves, storage failures swallowed deliberately and commented, opt-out kept in a separate key. Defects: (a) probe.mjs drains the whole response body (`res.on('data', () => {})`) with no size cap, so pointing it at a large .mp4/.pdf downloads the entire file for header-only work, with only the 10 s timeout as a bound; a HEAD or an abort after headers would do; (b) parseCacheControl splits on every comma so quoted-string values containing commas (valid per RFC 9111 s5.2) produce junk directives; (c) `Number(argv[++i])` for --timeout silently turns `--timeout abc` into NaN then the default; (d) `import.meta.url === file://${process.argv[1]}` main-guard breaks on paths with spaces or symlinks; (e) USER_AGENT in probe.mjs points at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects URL; (f) only HEADER_NAMES are read, so Pragma, Surrogate-Control and CDN-Cache-Control, which CDN debugging depends on, are invisible.
evidence.claims: Each claim checked against a file: 'RFC 9111 defines Vary: * as never reusable' (README, index.html JSON-LD and FAQ lines 25 and 44-46, why-isnt-my-cdn-caching-this.html line 24 and 92) -> overstated, RFC 9111 s4.1/s4.3 allow reuse after validation, and the FAQ says 'overrides Cache-Control and Expires entirely' and 'uncacheable forever'. 'Exit 0 when no danger' -> verified by running. 'Nothing you paste is uploaded' -> index.html only imports analyze.mjs and usage.mjs; no fetch found. 'Only an anonymous local count' -> usage.mjs stores event name and day only; backed. No-warranty and authorisation disclaimers present in README and CLI header. Stale: llms.txt links to duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo and the probe UA to monorepo-projects, while VENTURE.yaml says production is marisstella.app/cache-control-check/. Same-page claim 'public + Set-Cookie leak' is stated without the no-store exception the tool then gets wrong.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a developer whose CDN is not caching runs `node check.mjs https://host/path`, reads the report, pastes JSON into the page. Works with zero install. Useful for the two named patterns and for the diagnostic page. Limits a practitioner hits in the first hour: it sends no conditional request (cannot tell whether a 304 would work), does not look at Age/Cache-Status/CF-Cache-Status to show whether the CDN did cache, ignores s-maxage in advice, cannot flag Pragma or Surrogate-Control, reports a false danger for public+no-store+cookie (fails their CI gate), and downloads full bodies.
evidence.domain: Compared against RFC 9111 (4.1 Vary, 4.2.1 freshness, 4.3 validation, 5.2.2 directives, 5.3 Expires) and RFC 9110 (If-Range strong validators). Matches on: weak ETag/range, Expires<=Date as stale, max-age beating Expires, no-store making max-age moot. Departs on: Vary:* treated as never-reusable rather than 'never matches without validation'; public+Set-Cookie danger fired despite no-store; Expires-before-Date advice ignoring s-maxage; no handling of quoted-string directives; a 'danger' vs 'notice' split with no 'warning' tier for context-dependent cases. A CDN engineer would trust the notices but override the two danger findings by hand.

defects.what: Cache-Control: public, no-store with Set-Cookie is reported as DANGER (exit 1). no-store forbids caches storing the response (RFC 9111 s5.2.2.5), so there is no cookie leak; a CI gate fails on a safe response and a test (analyze.test.mjs:203) enshrines it.

Vary: * is described as 'never reusable', 'uncacheable forever' and 'nothing is ever served from cache again'; RFC 9111 s4.1 says the stored response always fails to match, and s4.3 permits reuse after successful validation, so a 304 can still save the body. Same wording is in README, JSON-LD, FAQ and the why-isnt-my-cdn page.
Probe drains the complete response body with no size limit; a large asset target downloads in full for a headers-only check.
expires-before-date ignores s-maxage precedence for shared caches and fires on responses where Expires is not what a shared cache uses; parseCacheControl mis-splits quoted values containing commas.

Stale hosting URLs: probe User-Agent and llms.txt point at duncan-haywood.github.io, production is marisstella.app; --timeout garbage silently falls back to the default; main-guard breaks on paths with spaces.

verdict: A small, honest, fully working tool: every README feature ran, 75 tests pass and caught a seeded off-by-one in the Expires/Date comparison. It is held below the bar by correctness and claims: of the two findings it labels DANGER, one fires on a response that is safe (public + no-store + Set-Cookie) and the other is described more strongly than RFC 9111 s4.1/4.3 supports (Vary: * blocks matching, but validated reuse is allowed). The suite pins the false positive instead of catching it. A CDN engineer would use the notices and the diagnostic page, and distrust the exit code. Scores are before any fix.
